evidence_claims.claim: Human factors should consider the job, individual, and organization together
evidence_claims.limitations: Two HSE products are not independent evidence; concept not a quantitative error forecast

evidence_claims.claim: Workload, interruptions, poor visibility and fatigue can increase error risk
evidence_claims.limitations: Scope is workplace human-factors study; no particular individual risk quantified

evidence_claims.claim: A selection slip and a mistaken plan need different safeguards

supports.location: Chapter 2 Understanding human failure and causes

evidence_claims.limitations: Taxonomy is simplified and does not assign a diagnosis for actual incidents

evidence_claims.claim: Outdated labels and circuit identity require evidence before field work
evidence_claims.limitations: Do not infer actual branch circuit routing from dated plan

evidence_claims.claim: Repeated protective trips do not establish a harmless normal condition
evidence_claims.limitations: Specific trip patterns are not diagnosed from generic guidance; professional review pending

evidence_claims.claim: Clear and current procedures and job aids can reduce human errors
evidence_claims.limitations: Same agency publication family; applicability to task requires design

evidence_claims.claim: Independent checking must challenge assumptions rather than repeat a signature
evidence_claims.limitations: Interpretive training recommendation; not a formal study of two-signature effectiveness

evidence_claims.claim: Fatigue and time pressure justify re-planning rather than improvising
evidence_claims.limitations: No numerical cutoffs or safe work-time prescription

evidence_claims.claim: NIOSH ranks elimination/engineering above administrative controls and PPE
evidence_claims.limitations: Hierarchy generic; does not license unqualified physical modification

evidence_claims.claim: Shift/handoff communication and maintained documentation matter to safety
evidence_claims.limitations: Residential documentation must reflect real changes; external case studies not reviewed

evidence_claims.claim: Incident investigation should examine conditions that caused error

supports.location: p. 15 error management and Ch.5 incident review

evidence_claims.limitations: Not a blame/liability ruling or quantitative safety proof

evidence_claims.claim: Homeowner questions can improve handoff without constituting qualification
evidence_claims.limitations: Permissions differ by jurisdiction; homeowner questioning is not field competence

description: Examines how workplace routines, misleading evidence, organizational pressure, and unusable procedures contribute to electrical incidents, and why stopping on conflicting evidence is essential.
